title: Car Fleet
prompt:
`n` cars head to a destination at `target`. Car `i` starts at `position[i]` with speed `speed[i]`. A faster car catches up to a slower one ahead and then travels as a **fleet** at the slower car's speed (never passing). Return the number of fleets that arrive.

**Example**: `target = 12`, `position = [10,8,0,5,3]`, `speed = [2,4,1,1,3]` → `3`.

Sort by starting position (closest to target first); a car forms a new fleet only if it reaches the target strictly later than the fleet ahead.

tests.note: front car arrives first, stays ahead

hints: Time for a car to reach the target = `(target - position) / speed` (a double).
Process cars from nearest-the-target to farthest. Keep the arrival time of the current lead fleet.
If a car's time is STRICTLY greater than the lead's, it can't catch up — it's a new fleet; update the lead time.

solution.explanation: O(n log n) for the sort. Going front-to-back, any car whose solo arrival time is ≤ the fleet ahead of it will collide and merge (so it doesn't add a fleet); a strictly larger time means it stays behind forever as its own fleet.
